title: Game Concepts Scripts Overview (Signature)
body:
Signature game concepts with full scripts. Every record in this edition is a complete original game concept — premise, mechanics, characters and levels — together with its script: dialogue, scenes and systems. All concepts are original, and none uses any franchise intellectual property.

The ten concepts in this edition span cooperative adventure, stealth trading, racing, farming simulation, mystery investigation, platforming, puzzle adventure, strategy, narrative management and diplomacy, so that the edition works as a design library as well as a set of playable concepts.

Scripts are original dialogue written for these concepts. Nothing here copies dialogue, lyrics or text from any existing game.

title: The Cartographer's Second Atlas
body:
Signature fiction — unofficial original game concept. Premise: The Cartographer's Second Atlas is a cooperative map-making adventure, Signature expansion set in the inland sea of Glassreach. The player takes the role of Wren, accompanied by Old Tomas, and the central goal is to chart waters that refuse to be charted twice. Nothing in this concept copies any existing franchise: the characters, places and systems below are original.

Mechanics: (1) a core loop of explore, gather and decide, where every decision changes the state of the world in a visible way; (2) a resource system tied to the setting — time, light, paper or tide, depending on the concept — that is spent and earned through play rather than purchased; (3) a reputation system in which non-player characters remember how the player treated them and adjust their offers accordingly.

Characters: Wren, the player character, whose skills grow through use; Old Tomas, a companion who offers advice, carries supplies and has a goal of their own that sometimes conflicts with the player's; and a rotating cast of townspeople, rivals and officials, each with a daily routine the player can learn and plan around.

Levels and structure: three acts — an opening act that teaches the core loop in a small safe area, a middle act that opens the full map and introduces the central conflict, and a closing act that tests everything learned in a single sustained challenge. Progress is saved at waypoints, difficulty is set by the player's choices rather than a slider alone, and the game can be completed in a single sitting or across many sessions.

Script — opening scene, in the inland sea of Glassreach. Wren: 'We have one tide, one map, and no second chances — so we had better use all three well.' Old Tomas: 'Then we start with the honest work. Mark what is true, and leave the rest for later.' Wren: 'And if the map changes while we walk?' Old Tomas: 'Then we change with it, and we write down that it changed. That is the whole job.' The scene ends with the party choosing a route together, and the game records that choice as the first entry in the player's own atlas.

title: Game Design Toolkit (Signature)
body:
Design toolkit for the concepts in this edition: a shared framework any of the ten concepts can use. Core loop: explore, gather, decide, and watch the world change visibly in response. Resources are tied to the setting and earned through play, never purchased. Non-player characters remember treatment and adjust offers.

Scripting toolkit: every script in this edition follows the same shape — an opening scene that states the goal in dialogue, a middle scene that tests the goal under pressure, and a closing scene that records the player's choice. Dialogue is written to be spoken, with short lines, clear stakes and one memorable image per scene.

This toolkit is original design material. It does not copy any existing game's systems text or dialogue.
